pairs.question: Quare rem tanta diligentia conservandam, argumentum viri, vultus gloriam, hominis praecipuam auctoritatem, ita obligasset, tanquam rem mediocrem, et ab homine sine confusione separabilem?
pairs.answer: Quia non erat mihi res alia dignior cujus interpositione, militibus proterve instantibus, possem plenius satisfacere.
pairs.derivation: Gabriel asks Count Balduin why he pawned his beard; the count answers. Stripped the asking-frame 'quaerit iterum:' before the question and the answer-frame 'Cui comes:' before the reply. Answer ends at the first full stop ('satisfacere.'); what follows ('Sed nec oportet dominum et patrem meum...') turns to reassurance about repaying, so it is cut.

pairs.question: Josceline, habesne aliquid, quod ego tibi non dederim?
pairs.derivation: Count Balduin asks Joscelin whether he has anything the count did not give him; Joscelin answers. Stripped the speech-frame 'Et iterum verbum continuans, intulit:' before the question and 'Cui ille:' before the reply. The reply is the complete utterance.
